newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed on rolling, pork bellies strong.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed on rolling, pork bellies strong.

text.p: CME hog futures ended mixed as a large fund started to roll long June positions into back months and pork bellies finished strong to sharply higher on a firmer product market, traders said.

Hog futures closed up 0.475 cent a lb to off 0.300 with June off 0.150 at 84.375 cents and July up 0.250 at 85.400 cents. Pork bellies ended up 1.100 to 3.000 cent per lb with untraded March up the limit on a bid while July was up the least at 91.050 cents. August and February posted limit gains early before slipping.
Start of the "Goldman roll", rolling by the Goldman Sachs fund out of June in the hog pit, made for mixed activity in futures late, traders said.

Hog futures had posted early gains on higher cash hog and pork prices Wednesday before values slipped on profit taking. Expectations that cash hog markets will be steady at best Thursday also offset the early technical buy stops that took nearbys to within 0.150 and 0.200 cent of old contract highs before falling, traders said.
Some traders look for greater hog numbers coming to market once farmers are finished with fieldwork while others note that overall hog numbers will contract as the summer unfolds.
"Once the corn planting winds down there is a feeling that we are going to get some increased numbers on hogs," said Chuck Levitt, analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.

Cargill Investor Services, Refco, Smith Barney and FIMAT Futures USA rolled long June contracts into July and August. In hog options, RBH bought the June 83 straddle and sold the 86 straddle early, pit sources said.
Pork bellies shot up early to limit gains in August and February on Tuesday's bullish weekly CME out-of-town storage report but values later slipped off the highs, traders said.
CME reported a net out-movement of 952,000 lbs last week from warehouses outside Chicago which compares with an in-movement of 333,000 lbs last year.
"The mixed cash market at midday took some of the momentum away from the futures," Levitt said.
USDA quoted cash belly prices "firm" at midday.
But Levitt said a strong tone to cash still persisted. "It's a firm market and it's moving higher, but I'm not sure everybody agreed with that between twelve and one o'clock," he said.

Locals and scattered commission houses sold late while commercials bought. Rand Financials bought late, traders said. FIMAT, LIT division of First Options, R.J. O'Brien, Lind-Waldock and locals bought on the initial rally while LFG sold, pit sources said.
